hook_text: Every number in the books has a home and a partner. Here is how to find both.
clip_script: The journals are rough notebooks. The ledger is a filing cabinet with one card for every account. Posting carries each number to its card. From the money-in notebook, bank goes on the left, and everything else on the right: sales, capital, rent income. From the money-out notebook, it flips. Bank goes on the right, everything else on the left: stock, wages, rent, equipment, drawings. A perfect mirror. Next to each number, write the name of its partner, the other account in the deal. The capital card says Bank: the owner's money went into the bank. Then close the cards like a till at night. Bank: R140 250 in, R56 590 out. Difference: R83 660. Write it on the smaller side so both sides match, underline twice, and bring it down on the bigger side for 1 April. That is the money the shop starts the new month with.
visual_style: Numbers lift off a journal page and fly to labelled ledger cards, landing left or right; partner names light up in pairs; a T-account balances with c/d and b/d lines drawn in.
pacing: A quick flying montage, a clear mirror beat, a slower balancing finish.
